properties.summary: Administrative violation issued on 3/14/2023 to GREYLOCK CONVENTIONAL LLC in Cumberland Twp, Greene county. 78a55(i)4ii - EMERGNCY RESPONSE – Sign - Failure of the operator to meet requirements of site entrance sign fabrication, color, size, lettering, wording, numbering, format, information and location.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: GREYLOCK CONVENTIONAL LLC
Violation Type: Administrative
Violation Date: 3/14/2023
Violation Code: 78a55(i)4ii - EMERGNCY RESPONSE – Sign - Failure of the operator to meet requirements of site entrance sign fabrication, color, size, lettering, wording, numbering, format, information and location.
Violation ID: 988099
Permit API: 059-24674
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Cumberland Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/14/2023
Comments: On 3/14/23 a routine complete inspection of the V Virgili 1 OG Well site was conducted. I was accompanied by Chase Ambrose (PA DEP). During the inspection the following was observed:-The entrance to the site is shared with the Meadows and Cree well sites. An Act 9 sign for the Meadows and Cree sites was present, however there was no sign present for the V Virgili well site(Photo #1).-A well tag was observed on the wellhead displaying the well and operator information (Photo #3). - The well and production equipment appeared to be in generally good condition (Photos #2-3).-Significant corrosion was observed on the production tank (Photos #4-6). No elevated conductivity was observed around the tank. -An earthen berm was present around the production tank (Photo #7). I called Kieth Eighmey of Greylock and informed him of my findings. The Department recommends that Greylock replace the corroded tank, ensure that approved secondary containment is installed, and post an Act 9 sign at the site entrance.A violation of 78a55(i)4ii is being issued for failure to meet Act 9 sign requirements.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to INFLECTION ENERGY (PA) LLC in Eldred Twp, Lycoming County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2/02/2022 to INFLECTION ENERGY (PA) LLC in Eldred Twp, Lycoming county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: INFLECTION ENERGY (PA) LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2/02/2022
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 944177
Permit API: 081-21472
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Eldred Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2/02/2022
Comments: On February 2, 2022, DEP representatives Brad Kline and Brooke Millisock conducted a follow up site inspection at Inflection Energy TLC Well Pad. The DEP spoke with Inflection Energy Zac Subra and Penn E&R Matt Tusing. At the time of arrival, Inflection Energy was excavating the area that was covered by the containment of the rented GPU. The excavator was digging about 8-10 inches where the containment set. Then scraping the top layer of soil where the ground was exposed to the weather. Penn E&R was screening the soil conductivity as the excavation process was occurring. Penn E&R had marked the area to be excavated with spray paint. The area of impact was about the same as the previous inspection about 25 yards by 10 yards. Penn E&R screened the soil conductivity over the southwest pad edge and did not have any elevated conductivity readings. Penn E&R was planning on collecting confirmatory samples today. Inflection Energy said they did find a small hole in the containment of the GPU when the GPU was moved. The GPU has been moved to another location on the pad and is in a polyurea coated secondary containment. No new violations noted. Outstanding violations remain from Inspection Report 3314913.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/04/2024 to DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC in Fallowfield Township, Washington county. 102.11(a)1 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS – BMP AND DESIGN STANDARDS - Person failed to design, implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation to protect, maintain, reclaim and restore water quality and existing and designated uses.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/04/2024
Violation Code: 102.11(a)1 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS – BMP AND DESIGN STANDARDS - Person failed to design, implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation to protect, maintain, reclaim and restore water quality and existing and designated uses.
Violation ID: 8182300
Permit API: 125-22817
Unconventional: No
County: Washington
Municipality: Fallowfield Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/04/2024
Comments: On 04/04/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Molek F19 Well Site following violations issued on 12/08/2023 (IR 3657799, Enforcement 419234). On 12/08/2023, violations of 102.11(a), 102.22(a)2ii, and 78.53 were issued as outstanding for the access road. Inspection from 12/28/2023 noted that the violations were still open, however the operator was in compliance with schedule. On 01/24/2024, the violations were outstanding (IR 3701625). On 03/11/2024, the violations were issued as outstanding (IR 3726997). The operator was in compliance with schedule on 03/27/2024 (IR 3736262).The following was observed during inspection on 04/04/2024:Inspection conducted after several large rain events. The beginning upper part of the channel was displaying accelerated erosion and rills entering the channel (Photos 1, 2). The opposite side of the road was displaying accelerated erosion and sedimentation. Sediment accumulation was noted within the stabilized area with establishing vegetation (Photos 3, 4). Upper culvert inlet was blocked with sediment (Photo 5).Several sections of the bank above the channel did not have temporary stabilization. A section of open soils was displaying rills leading into the channel. The channel was also displaying accelerated erosion and sedimentation (Photos 6, 7).The middle culvert was completely blocked with sediment. Gravel was noted above the inlet, flowing over towards the channel. Debris and channelization were noted leaving the culvert inlet (Photos 8-10).The outlet of the middle culvert had sediment accumulation within the grass and accelerated erosion below (Photos 11-15).Outlet of roadside channel was displaying accelerated erosion and sedimentation. It was noted that sediment and flow were also both coming from the direction of the Landowner's building, in addition to the site's channel. Sediment accumulation within vegetation leading to the collection box and the site's middle culvert (Photos 16-20).Sediment accumulation within culvert and the outlet. This leads towards the stream (Photos 21, 22).Several rills leading off site and towards the roadside channel near the beginning section of the access road (Photos 23, 24). Remnants of gravel/sediment noted leading off the beginning of the access road towards the main township road (Photo 25).The violations issued on 03/11/2024 remain outstanding. A violation of 102.22(b)1 is being issued for the lack of temporary stabilization and the associated accelerated erosion.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to THE PRODUCTION CO LLC in Jefferson Township, Fayette County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 9/18/2023 to THE PRODUCTION CO LLC in Jefferson Township, Fayette county. 102.11(a)1 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS – BMP AND DESIGN STANDARDS - Person failed to design, implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation to protect, maintain, reclaim and restore water quality and existing and designated uses.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: THE PRODUCTION CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/18/2023
Violation Code: 102.11(a)1 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS – BMP AND DESIGN STANDARDS - Person failed to design, implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation to protect, maintain, reclaim and restore water quality and existing and designated uses.
Violation ID: 8158799
Permit API: 051-24067
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: Jefferson Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/18/2023
Comments: On September 18 2023, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to IR 3491397, 3387914, 3514511, 3543627, and 3595504. The findings were as follows:According to the Order issued to the operator by the Department for this site, the Operator shall completely restore the well site within 9 months after plugging.The well site was not restored during today's inspection. The site was not exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. According to the landowner, the site has not been restored to pre-existing contours.The well was plugged on October 7, 2021 according the the plugging certificate submitted by the Operator for this well. As such, the Operator was to completely restore the well site no later than July 7, 2022. E and S Plan has not been received by the Department as previously requested in IRs 3262679, 3387914, 3514511, 3543627, and 3595504.No E and S Plan was found on site. Although there has been additional growth since the Department's last inspection in July of 2023, lack of adequate uniform vegetation is still observed due to multiple areas of exposed soil and rock. There are several bare spots throughout the former well site that are lacking adequate uniform vegetation. No E and S BMPs are installed on site.The ground appears to be seeded in most areas, but 70% uniform vegetation has not been achieved at this time. Vegetative growth may be hindered by the amount of rock and gravel on site. The Department recommends the Operator take necessary measures to ensure 70% uniform vegetative growth is achieved for restoration of the site.Based on today's inspection, violations shall remain outstanding.

properties.content:

Permit API: 081-21799
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Hepburn Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/28/2022
Comments: Weather was 22¿ and snowy at time of inspection. There were no Seneca resources representatives on location for inspection. Well had digital pressure monitoring equipment attached to the production tubing and the production casing. Production tubing pressure was 1215 psi and production casing pressure was 1359 psi at time of inspection. There were three annular vents plumbed to surface that were labeled 20 x 13, 13 x 9 and 9 x 5. The 13 x 9 vent had 100% LEL and 5% methane detected on it for approximately 1 minute before the meter went down to a zero reading. 0% combustible gas was detected on the other 2 vents, in the cellar or in the area around the well at time of inspection. No violations were noted at time of inspection.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2/10/2026 to GREYLOCK PROD LLC in Cumberland Township, Greene county. 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: GREYLOCK PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2/10/2026
Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 8264365
Permit API: 059-25724
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Cumberland Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/10/2026
Comments: On 02/10/2026, an incident inspection was conducted following notification of a spill that occurred on 2/09/2026 from Greylock (CTS #395045). I was accompanied by Madison Raviart (PA DEP Water Quality Specialist) and Greylock representative Trevor Wood. Per Greylock, the spill was reported to the Department's emergency hotline on 02/09/2026. It was reported that 1-3 bbls of brine water released onto the pad on 02/09/2026. The spill was identified at 4:00 PM and reported to the hotline at approximately 7:13 PM. Gravel and snow was impacted on the pad and the spill was contained to the pad and snow was hand shoveled into tanks containment. No waters of the Commonwealth were impacted. The following was observed during the inspection:The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance. There was no Emergency Response Plan or The Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency plan onsite at the site entrance (Photo 1). I recommend these be added to site near the site entrance. The access road appeared to be in generally good condition and maintained (Photo 2).Cinders were placed on road coming up to the pad on 02/10/2026 (Photos 3-5). Snow around the containment for the tanks was hand shoveled and put into the containment (Photo 6). The spill originated from a separator on the pad. High pressure caused brine water to come out of the separator and spray onto the pad and tank. 1-3 barrels (bbls) were released (Photos 7-10). Conductivity readings taken in the middle of the impacted area ranged from 2.09 mS/cm-4.55mS/cm (Photos 11,12). Conductivity reading taken in gravel on the opposite side of the entrance in front of separators was 252 S/cm (Photo 13). Conductivity readings taken along tank containment ranged from 709 S/cm-8.61 mS/cm (Photos 14-18).The area was still in the process of remediation and Greylock was waiting on additional equipment to begin remediation. The spill appeared to be greater than 42 gallons. I recommend following Act 2 guidelines.Due to the release of brine water and no Emergency Response Plan or The Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency plan onsite, violations of 78a.54, 78a57(a), SWMA 301, 91.34(a), 78A55(I)5I, and 78a66(b)2.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to MCCOOL JOHN E in Cherry Grove Township, Warren County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/17/2026 to MCCOOL JOHN E in Cherry Grove Township, Warren county. SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: MCCOOL JOHN E
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/17/2026
Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
Violation ID: 8278644
Permit API: 123-47075
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Cherry Grove Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/17/2026
Comments: This inspection is being conducted in response to the observation of production fluid exiting the secondary containment of the Lot 740 tank battery. Conventional well Lot 740 15 (API # 123-47075) is nearest the tank battery. The conventional well appears to be plumbed for production. An old sign displaying the API number, well name, and the wrong operator contact information is posted on a tree near the location. The sign should be updated with the current operator's name and contact information. The tank battery at the site has 2 steel tanks and a separator situated within an earthen secondary containment. The secondary containment was approximately 60ft x 20ft. Evidence of staining, dead vegetation, numerous deer tracks, and conductivity readings over range (greater than 20,000 mS/cm maximum that field meter can measure) were present in standing water throughout the entire secondary containment. This would indicate a large volume of production fluid filled the entire containment at one time (see photo 1). At the time of the inspection, the ground within the secondary containment was saturated with production fluid with some ponding throughout. A small amount of crude oil was also identified within the escaped production fluid. A containment drain inlet was located at a low point in the front left corner within the containment. A conductivity reading of 17.17 mS/cm was measured at the drain inlet (see photo 2). The ponding production fluid was flowing into the drain's inlet, exiting the containment through the drain outlet located at the exterior front left corner of the secondary containment (see photo 3). The containment drain was open and unattended at the time of this inspection. Sample 001 was collected at 13:10 at the containment drain outlet for further testing. A conductivity reading was also taken at this location measuring over range (see photo 4). The production fluid flowed from the containment drain into the road ditch traveling south approximately 50 feet (see photo 5). The escaped production fluid also flowed north in the road ditch approximately 10 feet before entering a road culvert where it continued westward into the woods for approximately 150 feet (see photo 6). The vegetation in the path of flow was dead, the ground was muddy and imprinted with deer tracks, and the conductivity readings measured high throughout the entire length of travel. The conductivity was measured near the apparent end of impact with a reading of 8.51 mS/cm in a puddle.The containment drain is required to be closed when unattended and the regulations state that any discharge is to only consist of precipitation that accumulates inside the containment, not production fluids. On June 18, 2026 a phone call was made to the operator, John McCool, in which he stated his intentions to work towards achieving compliance. He explained that the fluids currently stored in the tanks will be pumped empty and examined for leaks. If any leaks are identified, the tanks will be repaired or replaced. An excavator will be used to remove the contaminated soil within the secondary containment and beyond the containment drain exit following the path of travel through the woods. Upon disposing of the contaminated soils at an approved facility, a copy of the disposal slip from the landfill is expected to be provided to the Department. Confirmatory sampling will be required to confirm the impacts from the release have been sufficiently remediated. The Department's Policy 800-5000-001- "Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil and Gas Well Sites and Access Roads" sets forth the procedure to be followed to resolve the violations associated with the spill/discharge/release documented in this Notice of Violation ("NOV"), by using either the Act 2 or the Alternative Remediation Process. Follow up inspections will be performed routinely until the cleanup is deemed complete.

The ball valves were closed on all (20x13) annuli vents before there common vent line in order to isolate each annuli individually for gas checks being performed today for the beginning of the (SPBUTs).- Operator rep. (Tom Vitella) was on site to shut in the (20x13) annuli. - An ALTAIR 5X gas meter (cal.11/12/20) was turned on and gas checks performed @ the (20x13) Sentry valves showed no gas at time of shut in. - The (20x13) annuli were shut in @ 10:00, marking the start of the (SPBUTs). End of testing will be on Thurs. (12/3/20).

Comments: On 07/24/2024 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a routine inspection of Southwestern's (SWN's) Vanorder-Patrick (12 Pad) Well Pad in Herrick Township, Bradford County. The weather was 70 degrees and cloudy. Rain fell on the pad within the last24 hours. I arrived at 1035 hours. The site remains stabilized with greater than 70% perennial vegetative cover. There was no accelerated erosion or sedimentation observed. There are two post-construction stormwater management structures onsite. They appear to be functioning properly. Pooled water on the pad was field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) between 192.8-262 us/cm. There was no evidence of any spills or releases. There was one produced fluid tank held within secondary containment onsite. There were nine gas processing units (GPUs) held within secondary containment onsite. There were nine wells capable of producing. There were each properly tagged with the American Petroleum Institute (API) identification numbers. There were numerous temporary storage tanks held within secondary containment onsite. Violations remain outstanding at this site from a previous release. Site remediation has been performed and a Remediation Action Completion Report has been submitted to DEPs Environmental Cleanups and Brownfields program for review. The outstanding violations will be closed once attainment with Act 2 standards has be confirmed.The DEP recommends:1. Disposing of stormwater held in the secondary containment structures as soon as possible to maintain compliance with 25 PA 78a64a(e).I departed at 1135 hours.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/15/2022 to PENNECO OIL CO INC in Plum Boro, Allegheny county. 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PENNECO OIL CO INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/15/2022
Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 952052
Permit API: 003-22226
Unconventional: No
County: Allegheny
Municipality: Plum Boro
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 4/15/2022
Comments: On April 15th, 2022, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a spill incident reported to the Department for the Gospel Church Unit 10H Well Site in Plum Borough, Allegheny County. The Department reached out to Marc Jacobs of Penneco for additional information on the spill. Per Mr. Jacobs, the well tender discovered the spill on 4/15/2022. The spill occurred at a broken valve on one of the production tanks due to freeze/thaw. They estimate approximately 1 barrel of crude oil has been released and contained within the earthen dike. Cleanup crews have been called to the site. At this time, released oil is being absorbed with pads and peat soil until remediation efforts can continue on Monday. On Monday, 3rd party consultant (Woodard Curran) will be onsite to evaluate release. The affected production tanks will be removed and release area will be remediated. At time of inspection, several Penneco representatives were onsite finishing preliminary clean up efforts. Per Penneco representative, the release was discovered around 10am on 4/15/2022 by the well tender. The spill was estimated to occur sometime between 4/12/2022 (the last visit to the well site) and 4/15/2022. Penneco rep estimated release to be about 1 barrel at the production tank. A vacuum truck was onsite to remove surface crude oil from the release site. Rep stated that on 4/18/2022, two of the three tanks are to be removed and release area to be excavated. Release site was isolated within the dike around the production tanks. Absorbent pads and peat laid within the release area. The broken valve and pipe laid within the dike. There also appeared to be a release at the well head. Per Penneco Rep, there was a release of approximately 5 gallons from around the pump jack. Follow up inspection to be conducted upon completion of remediation efforts. The Department recommends Operator remediate impacted area IAW spill policy for releases greater than 42 gallons. The Department requests the following: disposal records/ manifests for removal of all impacted materials once available, quantity released at the production tank valve and at the well head, how quantity was determined, method of remediation, timeline of when the remediation will be completed, when the release around the wellhead occurred, why the release around the well head occurred and what was released at the well head. Based on today's observations, violations are being issued.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2019-01-30 to Pa Gen Energy Co Llc in Wharton Twp, Potter county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Pa Gen Energy Co Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-01-30
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 840721
Permit API: 105-21651
Unconventional: Yes
County: Potter
Municipality: Wharton Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-01-30
Comments: The DEP conducted an incident inspection of PGE's Pine Hill 1941 Well Pad in Wharton Twp, Potter County on 1/30/2019 at 1215 hours. The inspection was conducted in response to a spill reported to the DEP Report hotline by Nathan Harris (PGE). It was reported that at approximately 0900 a vac truck that was moving produced water from a production tank had "collapsed". The tank was estimated to have had 25 barrels of liquid inside when it collapsed. DEP WQS, Jonathan Pennings and I arrived onsite at 1215 hours. When we arrived the truck was still in place and crew was observed sucking up fluids from the pad surface. We observed the vac truck(see photo #1) and the impacted area (photo #2 & 14). Puddles and slush mixes were field measured with a PCSTestr returning readings ranging from ~2.0 ms/cm to ~15.0 ms/cm (see photos #3, 4 & 5). We spoke with Erick Duzick (PGE Completions Engineer) onsite who explained the vac trucks relief valve was frozen solid which had caused the truck to create a vacuum which in return caused the vac truck tank to implode. The truck driver reported that liquid was released from the back hatch and from a small hole in the side of the tank (see photos #10 &11). It appeared that most of the liquid would have released from the back hatch. The truck driver also mentioned that by the time he got a ride and another vac truck onsite, approximately 1.5 hours had passed before clean-up was underway. He also estimated (using the site glass) that ~25 barrels were in the truck before it imploded. The other vac truck driver that was onsite for clean-up explained to us that when he dropped off the recovered liquids at Clermont Storage Facility that he could let us know how much was recovered from the pad surface. Crew began scraping pad material when we were onsite. See photos #8, 9, & 12 showing the excavator and pile of impacted pad material/snow recovered. The material was then temporarily transferred to a sheet of plastic until a roll-off truck could make it onsite. A wrecker was also on the way to transport the vac truck. Observations made in the field confirmed that the release was more than 42 gallons. The operator should refer to the procedures outlined in 25 Pa Code Section 78a66(c)(2) pertaining to remediating releases greater than 42 gallons. Sample 0935-404 was collected by Jonathan approximately 10 feet north of the containment surrounding the production tanks. This sample was a snow mix from the pile of excavated material and will be submitted for metals only. We departed the site at 1330 hours. Due to observations made during the course of the inspection violations of the following are cited against Well Permit API #105-21651: 35 P.S. Section 691.402(b) 25 Pa. Code Section 78a.57(a) 35 P.S. Section 6018.301 Operator called on 1/31/2019 and reported that the clean-up was completed and screening of the impacted area was completed. Violations will remain open until remediation and reporting is conducted in compliance with 25 Pa. Code Section 78a.66.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/17/2021 to ARD OPR LLC in McIntyre Twp, Lycoming county. 78a66(b)1 - REPORTING AND REMEDIATING SPILLS AND RELEASES – Reporting releases – Operator or other responsible party failed to report spills and releases of regulated substances to the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: ARD OPR LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/17/2021
Violation Code: 78a66(b)1 - REPORTING AND REMEDIATING SPILLS AND RELEASES – Reporting releases – Operator or other responsible party failed to report spills and releases of regulated substances to the Department.
Violation ID: 920802
Permit API: 081-21885
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 6/17/2021
Comments: This admin inspection is in response to the receipt of partial analytical results for sample number 0718-177, taken on 6/7/21 as part of inspection number 3202448 on Pad B. Elevated strontium and aluminum in the analytical results indicate the release of a pollutional substance. In a call on 6/10/21 between Sean Vanfleet, DEP WQSS, and Rick Hall, representative for ARD, Mr. Hall said that there had previously been a tank containing brine on Pad B while the drilling operation was rigging up. He stated he found out from site personnel that the tank had leaked and released an estimated 20 barrels of brine onto secondary containment. Mr. Hall said that the berms on the secondary containment were not fully installed at that time and the fluid ran toward the area of the pad surface where sample 0718-177 was taken. Mr. Hall said that Creston Environmental screened the pad and found elevated conductivity in the travel lane where sample 0718-177 was taken. He said that the pad surface was scraped down to a depth of approximately 1" in this area. He said 3 boxes were filled with the excavated material. He stated that fluid with an elevated conductivity continued to seep out from beneath the secondary containment so a sump has been installed to collect this fluid. The remainder of the pad was also screened by Creston according to Rick. Creston also took a sample from the same area where sample 0718-177 was taken. Mr. Hall said that the company man did not initially report the release from the tank as he believed that the fluid had stayed on the secondary containment. Based on the estimated release volume, the Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation. Violations noted. Outstanding violations noted.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: OLYMPUS ENERGY, LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/30/2025
Violation Code: 78a64a(b) - SECONDARY CONTAINMENT – All regulated substances, including solid wastes and other regulated substances in equipment or vehicles, failed to be managed within secondary containment on the well site.
Violation ID: 8240287
Permit API: 129-29266
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Allegheny Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/30/2025
Comments: On June 30, 2025, the DEP conducted an Incident Inspection of Olympus Energy's Porter Well Pad located in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland County following a spill that was reported to the DEP hotline on 6/27/2025 at 2:37 pm.The spill report stated that at 1:15 pm on 6/27/2025, over 5 gallons of a produced water (Photo 12), fresh water, and frack chemicals (Photos 13-15) mixture was released on containment and on the gravel well pad at the Porter Well site.Accompanying during today's inspection is Olympus representative Laura Karosic.At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed an Act 9 Sign posted at the access road entrance with all required information posted on it. In the on-site mailbox, the DEP observed both an Emergency Response Plan and Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan, that had all required components.At the time of this inspection, zipper frack operations were being conducted on 2 Utica wells with 57 out of 153 fracks remaining.At the time of this inspection, Ms. Karosic stated that a hose connected to the blender ruptured spraying the mixture on and off containment, however no Waters of the Commonwealth were impacted. At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed the area of the graveled pad where this incident occurred to be adjacent to a fresh water impoundment located on site. The graveled well pad in this incident appeared to be scraped, the ground in this area was observed to be brown and muddy in comparison to the dry and gray graveled well pad surrounding this area. Ms. Karosic stated that 2-4 inches of the well pad in this incident area was scraped and vacuums were used to suck up any puddles of fluid. The secondary containment where this incident occurred appeared to be clean and dry.At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed 3 clamshell dumpsters on site, 2 were full of contaminated material and the 3rd will be filled with any remaining contaminated material once Moody arrives to conduct further remediation efforts.At the time of this inspection, the DEP utilized a conductivity meter to screen the graveled well pad. The DEP collected readings of 8.30 mS, 3.07 mS and 2.20 mS in the incident area and 8.21 mS underneath/at the base of the clean water impoundment. The area outside of this incident area where the ground was not scraped was also screened and the readings collected in that area was comparable to the background reading of 0.333 mS collected in vegetation by the Act 9 Sign. At the time of this inspection, the DEP notified Ms. Karosic of the elevated soil conductivity readings in the incident area and underneath the fresh water impoundment. Ms. Karosic stated that fracking operations is scheduled to commence between July 10-11, 2025, then the fresh water impoundment will be removed and remediation can be conducted in the area where the impoundment was located. The DEP recommends the Operator promptly remediate the release in accordance with 78a.66(c)(2).At the time of this inspection, Ms. Karosic stated that at this time they estimate that the quantity of the release is between 1 and 3 barrels and that they anticipate following Act 2 protocol for the clean up. At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed SDSs for all chemicals on site and included in the release mixture to be located in the on site trailer. Based on today's inspection, violations shall be issued for the 1-3 barrel release of produced water, fresh water, and fracking chemicals on the graveled well pad.The Operator is requested to submit a written response within 15 days of the receipt of this report. This response should include an incident report, a timeline, a plan for remediation of the violations and how the Operator quantified the amount released. The Operator will need to follow Act 2 guidelines as set by 78a.66(c)(2) and assess the impacts to the Water of the Commonwealth from the release.

In the on-site mailbox, the DEP observed both an Emergency Response Plan and Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan, that had all required components.At the time of this inspection, zipper frack operations were being conducted on 2 Utica wells with 57 out of 153 fracks remaining.At the time of this inspection, Ms. Karosic stated that a hose connected to the blender ruptured spraying the mixture on and off containment, however no Waters of the Commonwealth were impacted. At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed the area of the graveled pad where this incident occurred to be adjacent to a fresh water impoundment located on site. The graveled well pad in this incident appeared to be scraped, the ground in this area was observed to be brown and muddy in comparison to the dry and gray graveled well pad surrounding this area. Ms. Karosic stated that 2-4 inches of the well pad in this incident area was scraped and vacuums were used to suck up any puddles of fluid. The secondary containment where this incident occurred appeared to be clean and dry.At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed 3 clamshell dumpsters on site, 2 were full of contaminated material and the 3rd will be filled with any remaining contaminated material once Moody arrives to conduct further remediation efforts.At the time of this inspection, the DEP utilized a conductivity meter to screen the graveled well pad. The DEP collected readings of 8.30 mS, 3.07 mS and 2.20 mS in the incident area and 8.21 mS underneath/at the base of the clean water impoundment. The area outside of this incident area where the ground was not scraped was also screened and the readings collected in that area was comparable to the background reading of 0.333 mS collected in vegetation by the Act 9 Sign. At the time of this inspection, the DEP notified Ms. Karosic of the elevated soil conductivity readings in the incident area and underneath the fresh water impoundment. Ms. Karosic stated that fracking operations is scheduled to commence between July 10-11, 2025, then the fresh water impoundment will be removed and remediation can be conducted in the area where the impoundment was located. The DEP recommends the Operator promptly remediate the release in accordance with 78a.66(c)(2).At the time of this inspection, Ms. Karosic stated that at this time they estimate that the quantity of the release is between 1 and 3 barrels and that they anticipate following Act 2 protocol for the clean up. At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed SDSs for all chemicals on site and included in the release mixture to be located in the on site trailer. Based on today's inspection, violations shall be issued for the 1-3 barrel release of produced water, fresh water, and fracking chemicals on the graveled well pad.The Operator is requested to submit a written response within 15 days of the receipt of this report. This response should include an incident report, a timeline, a plan for remediation of the violations and how the Operator quantified the amount released. The Operator will need to follow Act 2 guidelines as set by 78a.66(c)(2) and assess the impacts to the Water of the Commonwealth from the release.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to ARD OPR LLC in Cascade Twp, Lycoming County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2/10/2021 to ARD OPR LLC in Cascade Twp, Lycoming county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: ARD OPR LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2/10/2021
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 907828
Permit API: 081-21846
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cascade Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/10/2021
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that drilling mud sprayed from a flare stack during a gas kick which impacted the pad surface and an adjacent area within the LOD on February 6, 2021. The site was snow-covered during this inspection. DEP EP Specialist Justin Abbott accompanied me on this inspection. We met with company man Bill Mitchell upon arriving on location. The rig is finishing the 2nd of 5 wells on the pad. The release occurred while the cementing the A-1H well. According to the company man on location, the drilling mud sprayed northeast of the flare stack. The mud spray landed on containment, in the travel lane along the northeast edge of the pad, and in the area within the LOD along the northeast side of the pad. Impacted snow was removed by skid steer and with shovels. The impacted snow was placed in a container for disposal. The mud residue could be observed on the well site secondary containment, on a battery of frac tanks, on several chemical totes, and on a light cover. No residue was observed on the pad surface or anywhere off of the pad. New snowfall the day before this inspection made an examination of the pad surface and the soil off of the pad difficult. According to an email sent on February 11, 2021 to the Department, Rick Hall of ARD stated that most of what impacted the snow off of the secondary containment was ash from drilling mud that was combusted by the flare stack. He stated that based on a minimal amount of fluid off containment, the small area impacted, and interviews with the company man and cleanup personnel, that the estimated release volume is less than 5 gallons. The Department requests a notification when the drilling rig is removed from the pad. Violations noted and considered immediately corrected.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to BULL RUN RESOURCES LLC in Lafayette Twp, McKean County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 5/25/2022 to BULL RUN RESOURCES LLC in Lafayette Twp, McKean county. SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BULL RUN RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/25/2022
Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
Violation ID: 956915
Permit API: 083-56364
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Lafayette Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/25/2022
Comments: This well was stimulated on 5/17/2022 and is currently being produced with a pump jack. The operator information is displayed on the pump jack. The pit used during the completion of this well has been reclaimed. Earth disturbance associated with reclaiming this pit and installing gathering lines alongside the spur road to the location has not been temporarily stabilized. A film of oil is evident on numerous trees along the southern edge of the location (beyond the pit). Stained soil with elevated specific conductivity (SPC) is also evident along various pathways across the forest floor downslope of where the pit was located. This is indicative that during the notching and/or frac'ing of this well, fluids associated with doing so were not sufficiently directed and/or contained in a pit. Two valves on the frac tank located at the southwestern corner of the well site are currently open and brine/production fluids are actively dripping out of them. Crude oil is pooled at both ends of the tank near the discharge points (valves) and the soil is stained for several feet downslope of each. SPC readings of the soil near the discharge points exceeded the upper limits of my field meter (20,000 uS/cm). Trees near the west side of the tank appear stressed as a result of the discharge from the tank. These observations are indicative that an appreciable (unknown) amount of brine/production fluids were released through the open valves on this tank. I contacted Justin Hansen of Bull Run and scheduled a field meeting to review these findings and discuss remediation options.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 7/20/2022 to PINE RIDGE ENERGY in Conewango Twp, Warren county. SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PINE RIDGE ENERGY
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/20/2022
Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
Violation ID: 962596
Permit API: 123-42860
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Conewango Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/20/2022
Comments: On 07/20/2022, The Department received a call from Brian Haner, stating a tree had fallen on a the well overnight and had broken the gathering lines. There was crude getting into a unnamed tributary of Irvine run. An estimated 2+ barrels made its way off site. Upon arrival on site Mr. Haner had booms across the unnamed tributary in several locations. There was a small under flow dam built on a spring seep just below the well. There were also several booms placed at the mouth of the unnamed tributary to Irvine run. Oil absorbent pads were being used to collect oil behind the booms. The crude made its way from the well pad down to a spring seep approx 10-15 feet. The crude continued down the spring into an unnamed tributary of Irvine run approx 140 feet. The spill then continued down the unnamed tributary approx. 1/4 mile. There is some evidence of crude in Irvine run at this time but it is slight. Rain is predicted over the coming days. We spoke with Mr. Haner about placing some booms in a better suited areas. Rain is predicted and the unnamed tributary is prone rise very quickly with small amounts of precipitation. The unnamed trib channel is boulder strewn and very rocky. He said he would move the booms around and monitor them going forward. Mr. Haner also had a excavator in route. He was going to get the impacted soil nearest the well dug up and into containers. He was also going to better construct the underflow dam that was built in the spring flow area just below the well pad. The under flow that was built was functioning but with any appreciable amount of rain it may not handle the added flow.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2019-06-26 to Repsol Oil & Gas Usa Llc in Columbia Twp, Bradford county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Repsol Oil & Gas Usa Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-06-26
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 853861
Permit API: 015-23288
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Columbia Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-06-26
Comments: The DEP conducted an incident inspection of Repsol's Bellows L (03-078) Well site in Columbia Twp, Bradford County on 6/26/2019 at 1130 hours. The weather was 79 degrees and mostly sunny. The inspection was conducted in response to a notice of the release called into the regional office. Kris Perritt (Repsol), Matt Bryan (Repsol), Andy Senefelder (Golder), and others from Repsol and numerous Bishop Brother's employees were all onsite. It was discovered that when the truck drivers were offloading the production tanks they were also taking water from the frac tank to top of their tanks. The tank was too low so when they would collect from the frac tank they were using the man-hole cover on the side of the tank to place hose through there to collect. This was reported to not have been properly closed. When the tank filled back up, production water was released from the cover. Upon this release, it was also discovered that the secondary containment around the frac tank had failed allowing most of the fluid within to be released to the pad surface. A reported 2 barrels was released. The release flowed into existing stormwater that had collected on the surface. In the area closest to the containment, I was obtaining readings of Over ranged on my PCSTestr35. Over Range represents a greater than 19.99ms/cm field reading. In the areas furthest from the release it was still clear that mixing had occurred and field readings of ~4.0-5.0ms/cm were still obtained. Repsol emptied the tank, removed it from the containment and marked the large area for excavation of 1-2 inches below the surface. Two vac trucks were deployed onsite to remove impacted waters. A dozer and skidsteer would be used to excavate pad material and dispose into roll-off tanks. A supervac(hydrovac) was also being deployed to excavate in the sensitive areas around the wellheads. A new containment was scheduled to be installed later today. Due to the findings throughout the course of the inspection, violations of the following are cited against API # 015-23288: 35 P.S. 691.402(b) 35 P.S. 6018.301 25 Pa. Code 78a.57(a)

Code §§ 78a.55 – 78a.58 and 78a.60 – 78a.63.

Code §§ 78a.55 – 78a.58 and 78a.60 – 78a.63.
Violation ID: 8202132
Permit API: 129-27964
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Salem Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/18/2024
Comments: On September 18 2024, the Department conducted a routine inspection of the Kepple 4H Well.The findings are as follows:At the time of this inspection, the access road appeared to be stabilized. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation issues were observed during this inspection. It appears a site ID sign (Act 9 sign) was previously present at the access road entrance, however at the time of the inspection, only the stakes/posts remain.The Department recommends the operator ensure an Act 9 sign is installed in accordance with 78a55. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP) and Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency plan (PPC) were present in the onsite mailbox.At the time of inspection, the well site appeared overgrown with vegetation. The well appeared equipped for production. A well tag was present on the well head at the time of this inspection, and a well posting was present on the GPU. The Department recommends updating the well posting to ensure all information in legible. There were no observed leaks or discharge of fluid on the ground or around the wellhead. One production tank was present onsite, however appeared to be unconnected and not in use. There also appeared to be a a another GPU behind the 5H GPU and the Department was unable to discern if it was in use. A barrel of methanol was also observed onsite and did not appear to be with in secondary containment. The Department recommends ensuring all regulated substances are placed with in proper secondary containment, and remove any equipment not necessary for production from the site. There were no visible leaks of fluid with the GPU and it appeared not to be in secondary containment, however the well was drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a. The GPU did appear to have signs of corrosion, therefore the Department recommends the operator assess the structural integrity all production equipment on site.While onsite, the Department spoke to operator representative Heather Empfield via phone call and discussed the Department's findings. Ms.Empfield stated she would get an Act 9 sign ordered and installed at the site as well as ensure field staff assess the site and correct any issues as needed.Based on todays inspection, violations are being issued for the Act 9 sign, observed corrosion on the GPU, production equipment on site not in use, and the regulated substance(s) not in secondary containment.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/12/2024
Violation Code: 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
Violation ID: 8201146
Permit API: 047-24934
Unconventional: Yes
County: Elk
Municipality: Jones Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/12/2024
Comments: I conducted this inspection in response to a spill that was self reported by Seneca. Seneca discovered three pin holes in the produced water line coming from the E08L pad. Approximately 10'x 20' x3' of soil was impacted by the release of produced water. Jeff Passarello from Seneca estimated that 25 gallons had been released from the compromised line. The leak was found during routine inspection of the line. At the time of my arrival crews had replaced the compromised section of the above ground produced water line and the excavated dirt was placed into 3 short containment boxes. These boxes are being temporarily stored inside of secondary containment on the E08L pad. Field conductivity probes were used to verify the impacted soil had been removed. Conductivity readings throughout the remediated area are comparable to background levels. 30-40 feet of brush was cleared to gain access to the failed section of pipe. A third party contractor was pulling up with a load of mulch and seed to temporarily stabilize the recent earth disturbance while I was on site.All removed soil will be disposed of at an approved facility pending lab results. Please provide proof of this materials disposal to The Department when it becomes available.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/05/2026
Violation Code: 102.11(a)1 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS – BMP AND DESIGN STANDARDS - Person failed to design, implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation to protect, maintain, reclaim and restore water quality and existing and designated uses.
Violation ID: 8267119
Permit API: 051-22184
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: Jefferson Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/05/2026
Comments: On March 5, 2026, the Department conducted a routine complete inspection in response to the operator's submission of a Notice of Intent (NOI) to plug this well.A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) with the Department was entered into on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, the Operator shall restore the site within 9 months of plugging. Stage of plugging operations was not confirmed during this inspection.E and S plans are present on-site.Access road appears to not have an RCE installed as depicted on the E and S plan. Some gravel/rock is observed, however due to its consistency throughout the entirety of the access road it appears this rock is pre-existing. Surface/vegetation disturbance is also observed beyond the width of the access road near the entrance. No CFS observed to be installed along the access road at this time.Erosion and sedimentation is observed along the access road at three separate points (Photos 6-17). Erosion channels are forming off the access road at all three points with the third one observed to be extending well beyond the access road downslope. No CFS is observed at either of these three areas. The Department recommends the operator install controls in accordance with the construction sequence and the E and S plan.Well tag and posting is not observed on site at this time.CFS on-site appears to be installed and functioning properly in accordance with the E and S plan (Photos 21-22).Violations are being issued for accelerated erosion and sedimentation along the access road, for failing to construct the site in accordance with the E and S plan, and for well tag and posting requirements not met on-site.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC in Lewis Township, Lycoming County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 11/29/2023 to RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC in Lewis Township, Lycoming county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 11/29/2023
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8166726
Permit API: 081-20763
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Lewis Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 11/29/2023
Comments: On November 29, 2023, DEP representatives Brad Kline, Erica Lutz, and Evan Buck conducted an follow up inspection at the Range Resources Cornwall Mountain 1-8H. This is to follow up with a reported spill by Range Resources on the afternoon of November 25, 2023 of approximately a barrel of production fluid. The production fluid was noticed bubbling from the well pad surface in the area of the buried dump line for the GPUs. Range Resources found a small hole in the the buried dump line from the GPU to the production fluid tanks during the initial excavation where the bubbling was occurring.Range Resources was continuing to excavate near and around the buried GPU dump line. The excavation area at the time of inspection was about 70 feet by 6 feet with a depth of approximately 5 feet. Range Resources was continually measuring the soil conductivity of the the area around the dump line. The soil conductivity in that area was approximately 3,000 uS/cm. Impacted soil was being placed on containment to be staged until a dump truck could be onsite to take the soil to the landfill. Kirby Steck with Range Resources said they plan to continue excavation along the dump line until lower soil conductivity levels are found.No new violations noted. Outstanding violations remain from Inspection Report 3650079.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to BLACKHILL ENERGY LLC in Springfield Twp, Bradford County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 7/07/2022 to BLACKHILL ENERGY LLC in Springfield Twp, Bradford county. 78a66(b)1 - REPORTING AND REMEDIATING SPILLS AND RELEASES – Reporting releases – Operator or other responsible party failed to report spills and releases of regulated substances to the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BLACKHILL ENERGY LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/07/2022
Violation Code: 78a66(b)1 - REPORTING AND REMEDIATING SPILLS AND RELEASES – Reporting releases – Operator or other responsible party failed to report spills and releases of regulated substances to the Department.
Violation ID: 961590
Permit API: 015-23678
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Springfield Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 7/07/2022
Comments: Follow-up inspection conducted to review operator response to NOV associated with inspection report # 3373528. Weather conditions at time of inspection are sunny and 81 degrees F. Meeting on site today with Cole Maxwell, Area Water Coordinator with Balackhill Energy and Kyle Jackson, Environmental Technician with Moody's Environmental. During this inspection an Elk Environmental Services water truck is removing produced fluid from vertical tanks at northeast corner of pad. Areas across the well pad have been scraped and excavated to remove soils contaminated with regulated substances. An equipment operator with Fenton Transport is operating a skid-steer with loader bucket, an excavator and a mini-excavator to remove impacted soils. 22 steel bins are located on site along with 3 vacuum boxes for vacuuming up puddles following precipitation events. Areas of the pad that have been scraped or dug for removal include soils around well cellars and a large area of the eastern section of the pad toward the produced fluid tanks and where evaporator concentrated fluid secondary containment was located. Test pits and shallow trenches have been dug near the east and west sides of the well cellars. According to Mr. Maxwell, the limiting factor for the cleanup operation is the hauling and return of empty bins for contaminated soils. A Hanna Groline Soil Conductivity probe and organic free reagent water were used to screen for conductivity on the pad. Areas to the east and west of well cellars and between GPUs and produced fluid containment continue to show elevated conductivity (photos 3 and 5). These areas were pointed out to Mr Maxwell and Jackson and are expected to be scraped as disposal bins become available. Cleanup activity is expected to continue until soil screenings indicate conductivity levels under 1 mS/cm.There are no new violations at this time.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/23/2026 to SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC in Middlebury Township, Tioga county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/23/2026
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 8278798
Permit API: 117-22231
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Middlebury Township
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 6/23/2026
Comments: On 6/23/2026, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an admin inspection for the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. This inspection is to report the results of four liquid samples that were collected during fracking operations from four locations at the site. During inspection #4183490 conducted on 4/21/2024, the department discovered instances of elevated conductance fluid on the north side of the pad surface, in the sediment basin below the north side of the pad and in liquid flowing past the LOD. Samples were collected from four locations. On 6/18/2024, the department received the results of the samples. Liquid in a 3' x 1.5' x 5" deep puddle, above the center outfall on the north side of the pad, field tested at 9.40 mS conductance. Sample 9551-242 was collected from the puddle. Reference pictures 1, 2, and 3.Liquid flowing into the southeast corner of the sediment basin from the rock lined outfall from the pad field tested at 10.30 mS conductance. Sample 9551-243 was collected from the flowing liquid. Reference pictures 4, 5, and 6.Liquid in the sediment pond next to the east overflow field tested at 3.04 mS conductance. Sample 9551-244 was collected from the pond. Reference pictures 7, 8, and 9.Liquid flowing north from the sediment basin, past the last compost filter sock and past the LOD field tested at 3.33 mS conductance. Sample 9551-245 was collected from the flowing liquid. Reference pictures 10, 11, and 12.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3846665 and ID 3855651 for puddles of water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin during completion operations. The DEP recommends that Seneca continues to monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered. Prevent elevated conductance fluids from leaving the facility and causing pollution to the waters of the Commonwealth.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to GEOPETRO LLC in Mercer Twp, Butler County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 8/16/2021 to GEOPETRO LLC in Mercer Twp, Butler county. 78a65(a)1i - SITE RESTORATION - Post Drilling - Owner or operator failed to restore the land surface within 9 months after completion of drilling all permitted wells on the well site or 9 months after the expiration of all existing well permits on the well site, whichever is later.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: GEOPETRO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/16/2021
Violation Code: 78a65(a)1i - SITE RESTORATION - Post Drilling - Owner or operator failed to restore the land surface within 9 months after completion of drilling all permitted wells on the well site or 9 months after the expiration of all existing well permits on the well site, whichever is later.
Violation ID: 926909
Permit API: 019-21992
Unconventional: Yes
County: Butler
Municipality: Mercer Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/16/2021
Comments: This inspection report has been developed to document an on-site routine complete inspect, and to summarize the overall status of this well and well location. The project was recently acquired by Big Dog Energy, LLC. Applications for the transfer of all four wells permitted on the site, from Geopetro LLC to Big Dog Energy LLC, were received by the Department on August 2, 2021. An application for the transfer of the ESCGP that is currently active on the site was also received by the Department. The current Operator information has not yet been updated in the Department's electronic database. Well Number 019-21992, along with three other wells, (API ID#'s: 019-21988, 019-21993, 019-22002), were drilled and currently exist on the location. Although the act nine sign has been changed to reflect the current owner of the well location, the well tags have not yet been updated. Updated well tags should be installed on each of the wells at some point in the near future. Inspection ID number's 2762573 and 2762664, (conducted in early August 2018), suggest that only well number 019-22002 was ever stimulated. Additionally, it was indicated that, at the time, RE Gas intended to plug all four wells beginning with the three that had not been stimulated. The wells were never plugged. An inspection dated 07/26/2018 (ID#:2769196) cites violations for failure to restore the well location, 78a65(a)1i and OGA3216(A). ESCGP number ESX12-019-0148 is currently active on the site. The permit was renewed by RE Gas in 2017 and is set to expire on 07/17/2022. None of the earthwork proposed in the plan was ever implemented in the field. The location consists of one very large well location and a separate tank pad. The location is overgrown and clearly has not been tended to in any way for some time. There are currently, however, no clear E&S or stabilization-related issues associated with the site.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/03/2022 to STL RESOURCES LLC in Grugan Twp, Clinton county. 78a66(b)2 - REPORTING AND REMEDIATING SPILLS AND RELEASES – Reporting releases - Operator or other responsible party failed to contact the appropriate regional Department office by telephone or call the Department’s Statewide toll free number as soon as practicable, but no later than 2 hours after discovering the spill or release.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: STL RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/03/2022
Violation Code: 78a66(b)2 - REPORTING AND REMEDIATING SPILLS AND RELEASES – Reporting releases - Operator or other responsible party failed to contact the appropriate regional Department office by telephone or call the Department’s Statewide toll free number as soon as practicable, but no later than 2 hours after discovering the spill or release.
Violation ID: 946419
Permit API: 035-21324
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton
Municipality: Grugan Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/03/2022
Comments: On March 3, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline, Brooke Millisock, and Clark Smith conducted a follow up site inspection at STL Resources Sturgis South Well Pad. This inspection is to follow up on a spill of 1,600 barrels of production fluid outside of containment that occurred on January 8, 2022. The southwest infiltration berm area of excavation has been uncovered and has filled with water. The water from the southwest infiltration berm area is overflowing the excavation depth and is flowing under a tarp. Due to the tarp covering the downgradient area of the excavation, the water overflowing could not be observed and could not be determined to be causing any erosion. The conductivity of the water in the in southwest excavation area was 104 uS/cm. The conductivity of the water in the southwest catch box of the well pad was 374 uS/cm. STL Resources continues to vacuum the water that has been collecting out of the catch boxes on the northwest and southwest corners of the well pad. The conductivity of the water in the northwest catch box was 7,800 uS/cm. Two seeps were observed near the northwest catch box, daylighting out of the slope of the well pad that had been previously excavated. The conductivity of the water in the seeps was 7,200 uS/cm. The water from the seeps is flowing in to an area that has been excavated and is covered by a tarp. The area under the tarp is a low spot in the excavation area the seep water appears to be contained in the low spot. Conductivity screening of the water in the remainder of the northwest infiltration berm excavation area resulted in conductivity less than 200 uS/cm. The DEP recommends collecting water from the seeps and delineating the area under the tarp for excavation of impacted soil. The DEP also recommends investigating where these seeps are originating from and installing corrective measures to eliminate the seeps. In addition to following up with the production fluid spill from January 8, 2022, the DEP did not observe any new erosion at the earthen infiltration berms noticed on February 28, 2022. The DEP did not observe any measures to correct the erosion that occurred. The DEP recommends adding temporary BMPs to these areas to help eliminate further erosion or to fix the earthen infiltration berms that had erosion issues. No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227, 3306834, and 3324293.

Violation Code: 78a66(b)2 - REPORTING AND REMEDIATING SPILLS AND RELEASES – Reporting releases - Operator or other responsible party failed to contact the appropriate regional Department office by telephone or call the Department’s Statewide toll free number as soon as practicable, but no later than 2 hours after discovering the spill or release.
Violation ID: 946419
Permit API: 035-21324
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton
Municipality: Grugan Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/03/2022
Comments: On March 3, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline, Brooke Millisock, and Clark Smith conducted a follow up site inspection at STL Resources Sturgis South Well Pad. This inspection is to follow up on a spill of 1,600 barrels of production fluid outside of containment that occurred on January 8, 2022. The southwest infiltration berm area of excavation has been uncovered and has filled with water. The water from the southwest infiltration berm area is overflowing the excavation depth and is flowing under a tarp. Due to the tarp covering the downgradient area of the excavation, the water overflowing could not be observed and could not be determined to be causing any erosion. The conductivity of the water in the in southwest excavation area was 104 uS/cm. The conductivity of the water in the southwest catch box of the well pad was 374 uS/cm. STL Resources continues to vacuum the water that has been collecting out of the catch boxes on the northwest and southwest corners of the well pad. The conductivity of the water in the northwest catch box was 7,800 uS/cm. Two seeps were observed near the northwest catch box, daylighting out of the slope of the well pad that had been previously excavated. The conductivity of the water in the seeps was 7,200 uS/cm. The water from the seeps is flowing in to an area that has been excavated and is covered by a tarp. The area under the tarp is a low spot in the excavation area the seep water appears to be contained in the low spot. Conductivity screening of the water in the remainder of the northwest infiltration berm excavation area resulted in conductivity less than 200 uS/cm. The DEP recommends collecting water from the seeps and delineating the area under the tarp for excavation of impacted soil. The DEP also recommends investigating where these seeps are originating from and installing corrective measures to eliminate the seeps. In addition to following up with the production fluid spill from January 8, 2022, the DEP did not observe any new erosion at the earthen infiltration berms noticed on February 28, 2022. The DEP did not observe any measures to correct the erosion that occurred. The DEP recommends adding temporary BMPs to these areas to help eliminate further erosion or to fix the earthen infiltration berms that had erosion issues. No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227, 3306834, and 3324293.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/18/2025 to COTERRA ENERGY INC in Lenox Township, Susquehanna county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: COTERRA ENERGY INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/18/2025
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8226353
Permit API: 115-20547
Unconventional: Yes
County: Susquehanna
Municipality: Lenox Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/18/2025
Comments: Casey Baldwin (WQS-DEP) and I arrived at the Zick J Pad 1 at 1045 to respond to a spill incident. Jon Sassi (EPS-DEP) was notified by Mike Oakley (EHS Specialist-Coterra) of a release of ethylene glycol discovered at 0738 this morning by a facilities foreman. Mr. Oakley reported that the foreman was on the pad to perform maintenance when he noticed a glycol smell and observed staining on the pad surface near the GPU for the 2H well. The glycol drum inside of the secondary containment barrel was rusted and caused the glycol to leak out into the secondary containment, which then leaked out of the containment barrel through a bung that was not completely fastened, and then onto the pad surface. While on site, Mr. Baldwin and I spoke with David Grosel (Lease Operator-Coterra) who informed us that all wells are temporarily shut in while they relocate the 2H GPU so that the impacted area can be remediated. Mr. Grosel also stated that Resource Environmental was on site earlier in the day to take a sample and would return once the equipment is moved from the impacted area. Mr. Baldwin and I observed the RLE wrecker relocating the GPU while we were on site. We also observed the remaining glycol being emptied from the rusted drum and into a Parrish truck for disposal.Mr. Baldwin and I then called Mr. Oakley for additional details regarding the release. Mr. Oakley informed us that the spill volume is currently unknown as they are still in the process of calculating the volume. He also stated that Resource Environmental will be on site the following morning, 3/19, to take additional samples and remediate the impacted area. They plan to soft dig to remove the impacted material as dump lines are present in the vicinity. On 3/19/25, Mr. Oakley informed the Department via email that the spill volume is estimated to be 47 gallons. The spill volume estimate was determined taking the difference between the working volume in the GPU (384 gallons) and the volume recovered from the unit, the overflow drum, and the overpack (337 gallons).The spill will be referred to the DEP NERO ECB Program for Act 2.Mr. Baldwin and I also performed a cursory inspection of the site. The well cellars appear to be full of fluid. Operator, please remove the fluid, per your plan, before the cellars overflow. Additionally, the vegetated filter strip on the west side of the pad was found to be lacking vegetation and had ruts and tire tracks throughout the area as well as hay bales placed within it. Operator, please rework this area to ensure it is reflective of your plan.Violations noted.

properties.content:
Report Details
