Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/10/2026
Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 8267125
Permit API: 111-20223
Unconventional: No
County: Somerset
Municipality: Somerset Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/10/2026
Comments: On March 10, 2026, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Oil and Gas Management's Neilan 1 well located in Somerset Township, Somerset County following IR 4106039.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a well tag fixed to the wellhead with all required information posted on it. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from the surface of the wellhead. Attached to this wellhead was a small metal production tank, no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the surface of this production tank either.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed some production equipment and a meter box on site. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this meter box or the production equipment attached to it.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed two other production tanks on site that both appeared to be connected to the well. The tank on the left did not have any observable holes or corrosive parts, however, the tank on the right still had several corroded pipes at the base of the tank and a pipe that was completely broken in half due to corrosion at the top of the tank. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near either production tank at this time.The Department obtained soil conductivity readings at the base of the production tank near the corroded piping. Readings of 0.74ms, 0.42mS, 0.56mS, were obtained. These readings appeared elevated in comparison to the background soil conductivity reading obtained of 0.09mS. It does not appear any remediation has occurred on site at the time of this inspection.Soil conductivity readings under the pipe were collected in the same localized location during the Department's previous inspection documented in IR 4106039 where it was 1.285mS. Therefore, since neither evidence of remedial actions were observed, nor a response from the operator has been received, the violations for a release remain outstanding as it appears the release may be diluting and/or migrating into the surrounding soil/subsurface areas.During IR 4106039, the Department requested the Operator submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of that inspection report. The written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, a plan for remediation of the spill or release, and how the Operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requested the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon its receipt. To date, the Department has yet to receive the aforementioned documents.Based on today's inspection, violations issued for a release from broken and corroded piping off of a production tank on site is remaining outstanding at this time.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 9/17/2025 to EQT PROD CO in Morris Township, Greene county. 78a55(i)5iD - EMERGNCY RESPONSE – Planning – Operator’s emergency response plan failed to include a description of the procedure to be used to provide the most current information to emergency responders in the event of an emergency.  Including the current Safety Data Sheet (SDS) required under law to be present at the well site, the location of the SDSs at the well site, the name of the position in the operator’s organization responsible for providing the information in sub clauses (I) and (II).
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT PROD CO
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/17/2025
Violation Code: 78a55(i)5iD - EMERGNCY RESPONSE – Planning – Operator’s emergency response plan failed to include a description of the procedure to be used to provide the most current information to emergency responders in the event of an emergency. Including the current Safety Data Sheet (SDS) required under law to be present at the well site, the location of the SDSs at the well site, the name of the position in the operator’s organization responsible for providing the information in sub clauses (I) and (II).
Violation ID: 8249214
Permit API: 059-27655
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Morris Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 9/17/2025
Comments: On 09/17/2025, an incident inspection was conducted at the Harden Farms Well Site following receipt of an incident report that was submitted to the Department on 09/17/2025 at 12:17 (CTS 392314).It was reported that 10 gallons of biocide material was spilled on site at 12:00, 09/17/2025. No waterways were affected. It was also reported that a clean up crew (SPSI) was on site.I called the EQT representative who reported the spill, Lance Witters, for information. I noted that SPSI arrived after I did, and I requested the Safety Data Sheet (SDS) to be sent to me. It was described to me that the material spilled was a Multi-Chem biocide. The cause of the release was that a hose back pressured, biocide flowed back to the tank, and the tank overflowed. It was estimated that 10 gallons spilled.SPSI had not began remediation and was not on the pad when I arrived. No personal were on the pad upon my arrival.The following was observed:The contaminated area was adjacent to the gas production units (GPUs). It was unknown if any production fluid was present in addition to the biocide spilled; no elevated conductivity was observed. No remediation had begun and SPSI was not on the pad when I arrived on the pad. SPSI arrived to the site after the Department (Photo 1). An extremely strong odor was experienced on site in the vicinity of the contaminated area.SPSI then arrived on the pad and had not begun remediation while I was on site. The impacted area was located between the well heads and the GPUs. The impacted area appeared wet with small sections of pooled fluid (Photos 2-5).I asked SPSI if they had the SDS, and they did not. The SDS was not located on site with the site documents in the mailboxes. I was able to locate a Control and Disposal Plan and the Site Specific Safety and Environmental Plan and Policy. I was not able to locate any information related to the Multi-Chem biocide (Photos 6-9). I also did not find a Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan (PPC) on site. The SDSs are required to be on site. The PPC Plan is also required to be on site during drilling or completion activities, however the well operator shall prepare and develop a site specific PPC plan prior to storing, using, or generating regulated substances to, on or from a well site.The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance (Photo 10).The Department requests a description of the activities that were being carried out that resulted in a spill.Due to the SDS not present on site, a PPC Plan not on site, failure to control regulated fluids with a release to the ground, and failure to use secondary containment, violations of 78a.54, 78a55(a), 78a55(b), 78a55(i)5iD, SWMA 301, 91.34(a), and 78a64a(b) are being issued.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/23/2026 to RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC in Nottingham Township, Washington county. 78a53 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL AND STORMWATER MANAGEMENT - Person proposing or conducting earth disturbance activities associated with oil and gas operations failed to comply with 25 Pa. Code § 102.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/23/2026
Violation Code: 78a53 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL AND STORMWATER MANAGEMENT - Person proposing or conducting earth disturbance activities associated with oil and gas operations failed to comply with 25 Pa. Code § 102.
Violation ID: 8268869
Permit API: 125-29232
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Nottingham Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/23/2026
Comments: On March 23, 2026, the Department conducted a routine complete inspection of the Sanns Frank well site. The inspection is separated into 3 inspection reports due to number of photos. This is inspection 1 of 3.The ESCGP (ESG076322011-00) for this site was issued on 8/27/2021 and was set to expire on 8/26/2026, but was terminated on 11/6/2024 (IRs 3862784 and 3863032).There are 8 total wells on-site at this time. The 1H, 2H, 3H, and 7H appear to be completed and equipped for production at this time. The 4H, 5H, 6H, and 8H appear to have recently completed drilling activities and are currently not in production.Act 9 sign is present and complies with 78a55 fabrication requirements. Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan, and ESCGP plans are all present on site. The ERP and PPC plans include the required components.Wet Pond (Photos 4-5) appears to be functioning properly, no E and S issues observed at this time.The area below the outlet and level spreader of MRC Rain Garden #2 (Photos 8-17) appears to be heavily saturated with lack of vegetation and exposed earth as the water flows towards UNT to Mingo Creek. The water appears to be exiting the level spreader in sheet flow, but appears to be channelizing as it exits the LOD into the tree line. At this time, the water is entering the stream but no active sediment discharge is observed.The access road crossing of UNT to Mingo Creek (Photos 22-25) is observed with CFS installed on both sides of the access road. The CFS appears to have been installed properly but appears to have not been maintained and is failing, allowing mud to exit the access road via undercutting. The mud is observed to continuing down the slope below the access road into a pond of water on the East side, which also continues via channelized flow into UNT to Mingo Creek. What appears to be dust from the access road is also observed on the surface below the access road on the East side and is observed on most of the leaf cover in this area. At this time, no active sediment discharge is observed into the stream.On the West side, it appears that the extent of the dust and mud ends within the rip rap, however some gravel is observed off the access road.The rock apron below Channel 8 and the level spreader below MRC Rain Garden #3 both appear to be discharging stormwater in sheet flow, however the vegetation below both features is heavily saturated and the stormwater appears to be channelizing closer to the tree line, where it eventually reaches UNT to Mingo Creek. This area also appears to be impacted by a two track trail. At this time, no active sediment discharge is observed into the stream.Additional vegetation disturbances are observed along the access road (Photos 7-9, 13). No E and S issues are observed in these areas at this time. The DEP recommends the operator stabilize these areas.A small release of what appears to be a petroleum-based fluid is observed on the access road near the mailbox (Photos 18-19). The DEP spoke to Scott Clark (Range Resources) during discovery of the release. Clark appeared to be leaving the well pad and informed the DEP that he was unaware of the release, but would have personnel clean it up today.The DEP recommends the operator properly dispose of the impacted material and requests the disposal documents when made available. No violation is being issued for the release at this time due to the volume of the release appearing to be below reporting limits.Well equipment on the well pad appears to be contained within secondary containment and no other spills, leaks, or releases were observed on the well pad at this time.Wooden stakes with ribbons attached are observed at several disturbed areas on-site and near UNT to Mingo. The DEP requests additional information in regard to the stakes.Violations for accelerated erosion and sedimentation, failed E and S BMPs, and failure to maintain PCSM BMP are being issued at this time.

Comments: On 3/28/2024 OGI Geoffrey Lutty attempted to conduct an onsite inspection for the Burkholder Joshowitz Unit 1 well, API 051-20841. Upon arrival there was no well at the original coordinates 40.041485, 79.664770 as seen in photograph 8. Two potential wells were located. One well was located 500' southwest of the originally provided coordinates at approximately 40.04452, -79.66384 as seen in photographs 1-7. The well appeared active and was unlabeled. Moderate corrosion was observed. No gas was detected using a Bascom Turner EGA 611. No well location exists at these coordinates on oil and gas mapping. The other potential well was located adjacent to the Columbia Gas Joshowitz Station R-47653, at 40.04452, -79.66314 as seen in photographs 9-13. It could not be determined if this was a dehydrator and separator for the gasline or if it was a well. The well was unlabeled but appeared active. Moderate corrosion was observed. No gas was detected using a Bascom Turner EGA 611. No well location exists at these coordinates on oil and gas mapping. The 2023 MIA and APR reports have been submitted but indicate no production and state production for this well is reported under 051-20513. The 051-20513 well is located and labeled at 40.02487, -79.6737. The reports further indicate the operator has no record of spudding the API 051-20841. As this well has not been used in over a year as indicated by the production reports, it is considered an abandoned well. The Department requests the operator conduct an onsite inspection for the wells to determine the location of 051-20841. Based on todays inspection the following violations will be issued: OGA 3220(A) - Failure to plug the well upon abandoning it. 78.91(a) - Failure to plug the well upon abandoning it. OGA3211(G) - Operator address, name, number, API, and well name not posted.

Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 7/01/2026
Comments: On July 1 2026, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in regards to violations issued under inspection report 4180776. This well is under Consent Order and Agreement (COA) 407094. The well was reportedly plugged on 2/27/2025, therefore the site shall be restored no later than 11/27/2025. Present during the inspection was operator representative Joe Miller.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection the Department was unable to locate a restoration plan onsite. Therefore, the Department was unable to compare the well site to the restoration plan. The Department recommended to Mr. Miller that the site restoration plan be present at the well site until the Post Plugging Well Site Restoration Report is submitted and approved. Mr. Miller stated he would ensure a copy is brought to the well site and remain there until the Post Plugging Well Site Restoration Report is submitted and approved.Upon inspection of the access road, it appeared to have achieved 70% uniform and adequate vegetative coverage. No erosion or sedimentation issues were observed at the time of the inspection. Upon inspection of the former well site, the Department observed an above ground monument for the reportedly plugged well. No other production equipment was observed on site. There were no observed leaks at the surface in the area surrounding the well monument. The well site did appear to have achieved 70% uniform and adequate vegetative coverage. No erosion or sedimentation issues were observed at the time of the inspection.The Department informed Mr. Miller that the site is to be restored 9 months after plugging of the well,and that the well was reportedly plugged on 2/27/2025, therefore the site shall be restored no later than 11/27/2025, and that the Post Plugging Well Site Restoration Report is due 60 days after restoration. The Department then recommended Mr. Miller submit the Post Plugging Well Site Restoration Report if the site is restored in accordance with the restoration plan.Based on today's inspection, violations associated with no erosion and sedimentation controls installed are being closed as the site has achieved 70% uniform and adequate vegetative coverage. The violation regarding no E and S/Restoration Plan onsite is outstanding.

Present during the inspection was operator representative Joe Miller.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection the Department was unable to locate a restoration plan onsite. Therefore, the Department was unable to compare the well site to the restoration plan. The Department recommended to Mr. Miller that the site restoration plan be present at the well site until the Post Plugging Well Site Restoration Report is submitted and approved. Mr. Miller stated he would ensure a copy is brought to the well site and remain there until the Post Plugging Well Site Restoration Report is submitted and approved.Upon inspection of the access road, it appeared to have achieved 70% uniform and adequate vegetative coverage. No erosion or sedimentation issues were observed at the time of the inspection. Upon inspection of the former well site, the Department observed an above ground monument for the reportedly plugged well. No other production equipment was observed on site. There were no observed leaks at the surface in the area surrounding the well monument. The well site did appear to have achieved 70% uniform and adequate vegetative coverage. No erosion or sedimentation issues were observed at the time of the inspection.The Department informed Mr. Miller that the site is to be restored 9 months after plugging of the well,and that the well was reportedly plugged on 2/27/2025, therefore the site shall be restored no later than 11/27/2025, and that the Post Plugging Well Site Restoration Report is due 60 days after restoration. The Department then recommended Mr. Miller submit the Post Plugging Well Site Restoration Report if the site is restored in accordance with the restoration plan.Based on today's inspection, violations associated with no erosion and sedimentation controls installed are being closed as the site has achieved 70% uniform and adequate vegetative coverage. The violation regarding no E and S/Restoration Plan onsite is outstanding.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/18/2025
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8249229
Permit API: 015-23945
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Monroe Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 9/19/2025
Comments: Incident inspection of Expand's "Lucy" Marcellus well site.Steve Moyer (Expand) called the DEP on September 18, 2025 (yesterday) to report an unknown quantity of brine released onto the pad surface that they discovered the same day.I met with Steve Moyer on site. Expand finished hydraulically fracturing the 6 new Marcellus wells at this site. He explained that while washing wooden mats yesterday on top of plastic liner they discovered a hole in the liner which leaked some of the wash water onto the pad surface. After removing the liner a vac truck removed pooled liquid from the pad surface. Then an excavator that was already on site to grade the pad removed the moist pad material in the approximately 50'x160' area and 1-2" deep. That material is now staged on felt and plastic liners and covered with plastic liner on the NW corner of the pad. Expand completed the cleanup the same day of the release. Crescent Environmental directed the cleanup and field verified it by testing electrical conductivity (EC) of the pad material. The impacted pad material had EC of 5-6 mS/cm. They also collected confirmatory samples of the material after the cleanup was complete. Chesapeake spudded 6 conductor casings here on October 9, 2024. Precision 569 ST-1500 drilled the 6 new Marcellus wells here December 17, 2024 thru late February 2025.Vegetation and rock stabilize soil of the site to comply with 102.22 Permanent Stabilization. Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. I did not see any pooled water on the pad surface. Moist pad material has electrical conductivity of 0.28 mS/cm with a Hanna Soil Test probe.Air temp 69FJLP

The Amcor 3HC was reported to have 45% gas in the (13x9) annulus when in fact the screening performed on (10/26/23) showed no gas in the annulus. On location today along w/ OGI Dave Schoonover to witness the conclusion of 72hr. Stepped Pressure Build Up Test (SPBUT) being performed on the Amcor 2HC, 3HC, 21HC, 22HC, Stine WYO 7H and Stine WYO 8H wells. Comments: Stopped to investigate this complaint of oil overflowing a tank. Alan Wolf (DEP) was present. It was evident that the plastic brine tank had overflowed (no top lid and oil residue on top of tank and on the sides). There was oil saturated hay inside the diking. There was about 3 to 20 gallons of oil still in the diking. There was oil staining on the high ends of the inside of the diking indicating a significant fluid level that was once present and had dropped. The metal stock tank #64411, was about 1/4 full. The poly (brine) tank was also 1/4 full. There was stressed vegetation on the outside of the diking in roughly a 12' x 3' area. The conductivity was high in this area (20,000 micro siemens/cm with soil conductivity probe). The soil conductivity probe showed areas on average of 5,000 micro siemens/cm inside the diking about one foot deep. The gas well was producing with the annulus buried. The well was tagged. It had house gas plumbed off the 4" casing at the well with two regulators and a meter.

Violation ID: 8200888
Permit API: 059-25626
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Center Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 9/09/2024
Comments: On 9/9/2024, I conducted an inspection at the Kentor Inc Well Pad following a produced fluid spill reported to the DEP Emergency Hotline by EQT on 9/6/2024 (CTS #383608). The spill was initially identified as staining on the ground that was discovered upon the removal of secondary containment for the Kentor 8H Well plugging operation. The spill was later updated to be greater than 5 gallons, but it was unclear the exact amount of produced fluid that was spilled onto the well pad.On site at the time of inspection was SPSI for spill remediation. SPSI indicated that they had remediated areas right of the plugged well, and a 30x60 foot area right of the plugged well was delineated by sandbags. SPSI stated that rain received on site on 9/6/2024 likely resulted in the produced fluid spill migrating out further across site. It was not clear at the time of inspection the cause of the spill nor how much produced fluid had spilled. A full spill delineation was not evident at the time of inspection. 2 rolloff boxes of impacted material were staged on site at the time of inspection, and SPSI was awaiting a third box to continue remediation.I spoke to Logan Dominick of EQT via phone call during my inspection who stated that the spill would likely be classified as an Act 2 Spill, and that the Kentor 8H Well was transferred to Leatherwood LLC to be plugged for mine-through.While on site I observed the following:-The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance and the access road appeared to be in generally good condition (Photos 1-3).-Aggregate staining as a result of produced fluid was evident immediately surrounding the left and right of the plugged well when entering the site. Aggregate was being excavated immediately around the plugged well at the time of inspection. I observed a range of conductivity readings in the stained aggregate surrounding the plugged well, varying from 2.18 mS/cm to 10.01 mS/cm. Standing fluid left of the plugged well appeared to have greater conductivity readings (Photos 4-12).-SPSI informed me while on site that they had discovered a soft spot in the aggregate on the well pad during initial remediation approximately 75-100 feet from the plugged well. Upon excavating this soft spot, produced fluid began filling up the hole. I observed conductivity readings of 10.01 mS/cm of the produced fluid standing within the hole, and the soil/aggregate read at 1859 us/cm (Photos 13-15).-Staining on the ground approximately 20 feet from the excavated hole with produced fluid within it resulted in normal conductivity measurements (Photo 16).-I observed conductivity readings of 5.65 mS/cm of standing fluid within the 30x60 ft spill delineation. Standing water located behind a black tarp at the edge of the delineated area demonstrated normal conductivity (Photos 17-21).-At the time of inspection, SPSI was excavating surficial aggregate/soil that was demonstrating overall conductivity readings of 4 mS/cm (Photos 22-23).-Standing fluid within a sump/trench dug near the left-side of the Kentor Well Site demonstrated normal conductivity (Photos 24-25).Violations of 91.34(A), 78a.57(a), 78a.54, and SWMA 301 are being issued for the spill. In addition, The Department is requesting Leatherwood LLC's Kentor 8H Well plugging secondary containment plan and the maintenance records associated with the secondary containment used in the plugging process.

Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8200888
Permit API: 059-25626
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Center Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 9/09/2024
Comments: On 9/9/2024, I conducted an inspection at the Kentor Inc Well Pad following a produced fluid spill reported to the DEP Emergency Hotline by EQT on 9/6/2024 (CTS #383608). The spill was initially identified as staining on the ground that was discovered upon the removal of secondary containment for the Kentor 8H Well plugging operation. The spill was later updated to be greater than 5 gallons, but it was unclear the exact amount of produced fluid that was spilled onto the well pad.On site at the time of inspection was SPSI for spill remediation. SPSI indicated that they had remediated areas right of the plugged well, and a 30x60 foot area right of the plugged well was delineated by sandbags. SPSI stated that rain received on site on 9/6/2024 likely resulted in the produced fluid spill migrating out further across site. It was not clear at the time of inspection the cause of the spill nor how much produced fluid had spilled. A full spill delineation was not evident at the time of inspection. 2 rolloff boxes of impacted material were staged on site at the time of inspection, and SPSI was awaiting a third box to continue remediation.I spoke to Logan Dominick of EQT via phone call during my inspection who stated that the spill would likely be classified as an Act 2 Spill, and that the Kentor 8H Well was transferred to Leatherwood LLC to be plugged for mine-through.While on site I observed the following:-The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance and the access road appeared to be in generally good condition (Photos 1-3).-Aggregate staining as a result of produced fluid was evident immediately surrounding the left and right of the plugged well when entering the site. Aggregate was being excavated immediately around the plugged well at the time of inspection. I observed a range of conductivity readings in the stained aggregate surrounding the plugged well, varying from 2.18 mS/cm to 10.01 mS/cm. Standing fluid left of the plugged well appeared to have greater conductivity readings (Photos 4-12).-SPSI informed me while on site that they had discovered a soft spot in the aggregate on the well pad during initial remediation approximately 75-100 feet from the plugged well. Upon excavating this soft spot, produced fluid began filling up the hole. I observed conductivity readings of 10.01 mS/cm of the produced fluid standing within the hole, and the soil/aggregate read at 1859 us/cm (Photos 13-15).-Staining on the ground approximately 20 feet from the excavated hole with produced fluid within it resulted in normal conductivity measurements (Photo 16).-I observed conductivity readings of 5.65 mS/cm of standing fluid within the 30x60 ft spill delineation. Standing water located behind a black tarp at the edge of the delineated area demonstrated normal conductivity (Photos 17-21).-At the time of inspection, SPSI was excavating surficial aggregate/soil that was demonstrating overall conductivity readings of 4 mS/cm (Photos 22-23).-Standing fluid within a sump/trench dug near the left-side of the Kentor Well Site demonstrated normal conductivity (Photos 24-25).Violations of 91.34(A), 78a.57(a), 78a.54, and SWMA 301 are being issued for the spill. In addition, The Department is requesting Leatherwood LLC's Kentor 8H Well plugging secondary containment plan and the maintenance records associated with the secondary containment used in the plugging process.

properties.content:
Report Details
Operator Devonian Resources Inc
Violation Type Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date 2017-03-01
Violation Code 91.33(A) - INCIDENTS CAUSING OR THREATENING POLLUTION - Failure to notify the Department of an accident or other activity or incident, a toxic substance or another substance which would endanger downstream users of the waters, result in pollution or create a danger of pollution of the waters of this Commonwealth, or would damage property.
Violation ID 779888
Permit API 065-26057
Unconventional N
County Jefferson
Municipality Henderson Twp
Inspection Type Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date 2017-02-28
Comments This well was drilled in an agricultural area off of Cider Mill Road in November 2007. The well is equipped for production with a brine tank attached, and has been tagged with the correct DEP permit number. The site had been graded to final contours and returned to its original use as a farm field. Vegetation has stabilized the perimeter of the well site. A spill had occurred at the site when the 50 bbl poly brine tank had overflowed. Since the most recent inspection on 1/18/2017 (Inspection Record # 2553367), work on correcting the violations has started. Conductivity readings from the water in the area of excavation were approximately 300 umHos/cm, and the pH was approximately 8.8. The brine tank was empty at the time of inspection. Because the amount of released production fluid is estimated to be over 5 gallons but less than 1 bbl, a visual cleanup of this site is under way. The well is located approximately 430' from its originally permitted location. A revised platt showing the actual location of the well has been recieved by the Department, and this issue has been corrected. Contaminated soil has been excavated from the spill site, and placed on and under plastic near the well equipment. This material must be removed from the site, and manifest & tipping receipts related to disposal must be received by the Department. When this information is received, the remaining violations can be closed. Clean up continues. Violation IDs 771665 and 776748 have been closed. Violation IDs from the initial NOV dated 11/1/2016 that remain open: 771660 771661 771662 771663 771664 Violation IDs from the OUTST inspection dated 1/18/2017 that remain open: 776743 776744 776745 776746 776747 This violation remains open, but can be closed when the material is removed from the site, and requested tipping receipts and manifest information is received by the Department.

properties.summary: Administrative violation issued on 12/21/2022 to NUCOMER ENERGY LLC in Pymatuning Twp, Mercer county. 78.88(e) - OPERATING WELLS - MECHANICAL INTEGRITY OF OPERATING WELLS - Operator failed to submit an annual report to the Department identifying the compliance status of each well with the mechanical integrity requirements for structurally sound wells in compliance with 25 Pa. Code Section 78.73(c).
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: NUCOMER ENERGY LLC
Violation Type: Administrative
Violation Date: 12/21/2022
Violation Code: 78.88(e) - OPERATING WELLS - MECHANICAL INTEGRITY OF OPERATING WELLS - Operator failed to submit an annual report to the Department identifying the compliance status of each well with the mechanical integrity requirements for structurally sound wells in compliance with 25 Pa. Code Section 78.73(c).
Violation ID: 979545
Permit API: 085-23691
Unconventional: No
County: Mercer
Municipality: Pymatuning Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/21/2022
Comments: Routine field inspection performed in afternoon with cold, partly sunny weather conditions, and 32 degrees. Last inspection performed on 8/1/21, more than 1 year ago. Wellhead is located in partially wooded area along cleared access pathway ~250' South of surface/ground production equipment (photo #1). The wellhead is in fairly close, but not visible proximity to the production facility (photo #2). At the wellhead the surface casing valve is open, lower right side production tubular valve closed to port, lower production tubular left side valve is open, upper production tubular is plumbed with no valve unions, left side of head plumbed tubular to sales/surface equipment has open valve; annulus is buried, unable to determine if vented (photo #3). A functioning pressure gauge present atop upper production tubular left of head plumbed to sales/production recording ~115 psi (photo #4). Well label/marker is affixed to wellhead on lubricator (photo #5). The wellhead is in fairly close, but not visible proximity to the production facility and requires a well label/marker (photos #2 and #5). Some trace to occasionally moderate corrosion at the wellhead on the production/surface casing steel unions, lubricator, and tubulars. The surface/ground production facility and one 50 bbl poly tank all contained by a shallow earthen dike (photo #6). Valve closed on main tubular feeding facility but open valves to and from separator (photo #7). A 31-day production chart is present, with cycling markings dated 9/2/22 (photo #8). No Well posting signage is affixed anywhere at facility. Notice of Violation issued on 12/12/2019 for Well posting OGA3211(G) continues and is outstanding. Fair to occasionally moderate corrosion on ground production unit equipment. Continued Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Well posting OGA3211(G). The Department is requesting Operator add contact address information to the permanent well posting signage affixed at the surface production facility. The Operator has not submitted 2021 Mechanical Integrity Assessment (MIA) for this well. No MIA submitted by the Operator for 2021, 2020, and 2019. The last MIA value officially submitted was back in 2018 stating 55 psig. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Operating Wells - Mechanical Integrity reporting 78.88(e). The Operator submitted annual production reported (APR) in 2021 of 0 Mcf recorded over 365 days. The 2021 annual production report submitted indicates that this well was not in production during the 2021 production year. Additionally, this well was noted as having 0 or blank production values under the gas and/or oil quantity columns and noted as Well Temporarily Not Producing under the non production comments columns of the 2021 and 2020 production reports. The last reported production value was in 2019 of 2,701 Mcf recorded over 365 days. This well appears to be back in production based on this inspection, the chart at facility with recordings, and the open valves at wellhead and separator.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 5/07/2024 to STONEHAVEN ENERGY MGT CO LLC in Henderson Township, Jefferson county. OGA3220(A) - PLUGGING REQUIREMENTS - Failure to plug the well upon abandoning it.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: STONEHAVEN ENERGY MGT CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/07/2024
Violation Code: OGA3220(A) - PLUGGING REQUIREMENTS - Failure to plug the well upon abandoning it.
Violation ID: 8186883
Permit API: 065-25991
Unconventional: No
County: Jefferson
Municipality: Henderson Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/07/2024
Comments: This well was drilled in an agricultural area off of Cider Mill Road in December 2007.On 10/24/22, an NOV was issued to Stonehaven Energy when it was discovered that the brine tank had been allowed to overflow. On 3/27/23, an administrative order was issued due to a lack of remedial action from Stonehaven Energy. This order was delivered in person by Bureau of Investigations staff on 3/28/2023. As per this administrative order, a written remediation plan was to be submitted to the Department by 5/26/23, and a final remediation report is to be submitted by 12/31/23. No remediation plans have been received by the Department as of this date. A Petition to Enforce was filed in Commonwealth Court on 8/16/2023. In response to that petition, a Commonwealth Order was issued on 12/13/2023 requiring a RemediationSchedule to be submitted to the Department within 60 days. As of this date, no Remediation Schedule has been received.During an inspection of the site on 4/20/23, it was noted that a partial soil excavation had occurred. At the time of this inspection, it does not appear that any further excavation has occurred since that date. The well has been tagged with the correct DEP permit number. The well valves were closed at the time of inspection, and the 50 bbl brine tank appears to be empty. The original violations regarding the spill at the site have been superseded by the administrative order.Since the most recent inspection of this site on 2/21/2024 (Inspection Record # 3715790) there have been no changes at the site. The outstanding violations at this site remain open and are unresolved.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to DIAMOND ENERGY PARTNERS LLC in New Vernon Twp, Mercer County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 5/02/2022 to DIAMOND ENERGY PARTNERS LLC in New Vernon Twp, Mercer county. SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIAMOND ENERGY PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/02/2022
Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
Violation ID: 954018
Permit API: 085-22185
Unconventional: No
County: Mercer
Municipality: New Vernon Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/02/2022
Comments: Responded to an oil spill at this gas well location. The plug for the heater tube in the stock tank failed and allowed oil to leak out of the tank and into the diking. With the recent heavy rains, it appears the fluid in the diking overflowed through an open freshwater drain pipe and an inadequate diking height in spots. There was a ditch located on the backside of the diking where some of the oil flowed into but most of the oil appears to have gone out the freshwater drain pipe and then down the lease road. The lease road was approximately 55 yards long and pockets of oil were located throughout it and then into the weeds heading towards that same ditch that runs parallel to the lease road. The ditch empties into the Lake Wilhelm Road ditch. This Lake Wilhelm Road ditch just had a sheen of oil of oil on it west of the driveway. The last spot oil was seen in this ditch was about 10 yards east of the driveway culvert pipe outfall. No oil or sheen was seen emptying into or in the main stream of Calvin Clark Run itself. The oil was mostly contained with sorbent pads and by the grass and brush in the ditch. Based on site observations, it appears that less than 1 bbl of oil was released outside the diking area. With the heavy rains predicted again in the next 2 days, it was suggested for them to install a siphon dam in the field ditch right before it enters into the road ditch. A small excavator arrived on site and was in the process of doing this when I left. They were getting a vac truck out there today to remove all the fluid in the tank to stop the leaking of the oil. At 3:31 PM, Matt Kleese from Diamond Energy called me. He reported that they had just removed around 50 bbls of old motor oil from that stock tank. He said this well produces very little fluid and it was definitely old oil (he thinks motor oil). So he feels somebody had apparently dumped old motor oil in this tank. He said that he is probably going to file a police report on this incident.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC in Columbia Township, Bradford County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/11/2024 to REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC in Columbia Township, Bradford county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/11/2024
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8182780
Permit API: 015-23838
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Columbia Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/11/2024
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a routine inspection of Repsol's Crank (03-067) O well site located in Columbia Township, Bradford County on 4/11/2024 at 0900 hours. The weather was 56 degrees F with cloudy skies and light rain. Rain fell onsite within the past 24 hours as well. An Act 9 sign is located at the site entrance.The site remains set-up for flow back activities. Crews worked today preparing equipment for site removal and recovering fluids within secondary containments and temporary storage tanks. Secondary containment structures remain in working condition with no evidence of leaking observed. The majority of the areas surrounding the well pad remain permanently stabilized with vegetated cover. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation was observed. Pooled fluids on the pad surface were field measured for electrical conductivity ranging from 570 to 1800us/cm. There was no evidence of spills/releases observed outside of secondary containment. On 3/20/2024, outlined within inspection report #3730668, the DEP observed elevated conductivity fluids pooled on the pad surface field measured at ~5.56mS/cm. Based on the elevated conductivity reading, the DEP collected a sample for standard analysis code 942 (Sample #0983-421). The analytical results from that sample are attached to this inspection report as photos and a file. The findings were reported to Repsol who promptly dispatched an environmental team to collect samples and a water truck to recover the fluid. During today's inspection, the elevated conductivity fluids were determined to have been removed and current fluid in the area was field measured for electrical conductivity at ~890us/cm. Based on the analytical sample results from sample #0983-421 and Repsol's timely response for remediation, violations of the following are cited as immediately corrected against API #015-23838:35 P.S. 691.402(b)35 P.S. 6018.30125 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)The DEP recommends the following:-Recovering the fluid held within the produced water tanks' secondary containment-Recovering the fluid held within the produced water tanks' smaller offload containment-Conducting necessary earth work to return the two smaller leveled surfaces near the entrance to pre-construction conditions and seeding/temporarily stabilizing No additional violations are cited at this time. I departed the site at 1045 hours.
